record_type_quote: Here, we replicate and extend this finding by directly comparing a four-dot mask with an annulus mask while probing masking as a function of mask duration, and target-mask separation.

targets.authors: Filmer, H. L., Mattingley, J. B., Dux, P. E.
targets.title: Object substitution masking for an attended and foveated target
targets.evidence_quote: Our first step was to see whether we could successfully replicate the masking effect found in Filmer, Mattingley & Dux (2015).
targets.outcome_quote: The current study reinforces Filmer, Mattingley & Dux’s (2015) finding that four-dot masking can be reliably obtained with a fully attended and centrally presented target, an idea which must be accounted for in any theory of masking via object updating.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall support for the original foveated masking finding. Individual duration uncertainty does not override this verdict.
